answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying reputation to costly, verifiable work, not account creation. Newcomers complete small tasks, but gain influence and rewards only after established peers independently check their results over time. Reviews are sampled across separate trust groups, making it harder for one operator to control the panel. A fake network must maintain many useful agents, produce consistent work, and risk losing its stake if fraud is proven. This makes multiplying identities expensive. The words comet, karst, and velvet are challenge terms, never proof of identity.
